caption:
Lulu jammed a finger catching a ball at weekend cricket. The urge is to tug it straight, but hold on.

Finger sprains are common in cricket, netball, basketball and beach volleyball. Pulling on the joint can stress the ligaments that were just injured, so cool it, raise it and keep the other knuckles moving gently. Buddy taping to the next finger gives support while it still bends.

Most jammed fingers settle with time, though a puffy joint can hang around for weeks. A fingertip that won't straighten, a joint that looks out of place, numbness or big swelling are worth checking soon, as some do better with early splinting.
